code:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.GetOrdersByCustomer
  @CustomerID INT
AS
SELECT * FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader
WHERE CustomerID = @CustomerID;

-- first call: @CustomerID=29825 (5 orders)
--   -> compiles a cheap Nested Loops plan
-- cached plan then reused for
--   @CustomerID=11000 (12,000 orders) -- badly
caption: Compiled once, for one value; reused for every value after.

code:
OPTION (RECOMPILE)

Forces a fresh compile using THIS call's
actual parameter value, bypassing cache.

Still bad after that, with current stats?
  -> not sniffing, something else is wrong.
Dramatically better?
  -> confirmed: parameter sniffing.
caption: This is what tells sniffing apart from stale statistics.
